description_full: Eldorado Gold Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the mining, exploration, development, and sale of mineral products primarily in Turkey, Canada, and Greece. It primarily produces gold, as well as silver, lead, and zinc. The company holds a 100% interest in the Kisladag and Efemçukuru mines located in Turkey; Lamaque complex located in Quebec, Canada; Olympias located in northern Greece; and Stratoni, Skouries, Perama Hill, and Sapes gold mines located in Greece. The company was formerly known as Eldorado Corporation Ltd. and changed its name to Eldorado Gold Corporation in April 1996. Eldorado Gold Corporation was incorporated in 1996 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: Eldorado Gold Corporation is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $8.2B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +28% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 29%.
The business throws off $235M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.4× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 23× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
